rubric.title: Rubric (v3, POV-aligned)

factors.name: A: Product pull, no sales machine
factors.earns: Inbound, PLG, open-source, marketplace or channel-driven growth with a tiny or absent sales team; real customer logos acquired without S&M. This is the gap Elsewhere's operating bench monetizes and the single strongest signal in their portfolio.
factors.loses: Outbound-built growth; POC-dependent selling; channel dependency on a single partner; growth that needs paid acquisition to continue.

factors.name: B: Fund III financial fit
factors.earns: $5M+ ARR (or a secondary-heavy structure that makes a $20-50M majority check price sanely); Rule of 40; recurring revenue quality (GRR first, NRR second); capital efficiency; evidence quality (company-stated or filed beats podcast beats third-party models).
factors.loses: Below $5M ARR without a secondary; services or one-time revenue in 'ARR'; founder-attested numbers with no corroboration; contradicted numbers; single-customer concentration above 25%.

factors.name: C: Operator-transplant readiness
factors.earns: Founder will become CPO/CTO under an installed CEO, or accept an OA Executive Chair; GTM gap is one an infra/security/MSP bench can fill; founders who have exited before; explicit transition plans.
factors.loses: Founder wants capital not a partner; 'prefer to retain control'; key-person risk without a transition path; a founder who wants to keep selling the way they sell today.

factors.name: D: Sector + AI-era durability
factors.earns: Portfolio-proven sectors in priority order: IT infrastructure/DevOps/monitoring > security > healthcare IT with a bench operator > business applications. AI makes the product more necessary (proprietary data, identity/data-layer control, agent-era tooling). Consolidating category with active acquirers.
factors.loses: Core capability is what LLMs commoditize; same feature shipping free or bundled by a platform the customer already pays; buyer budgets contracting; capital asymmetry vs funded rivals; no right-to-win beyond the current catalyst.

factors.name: E: Deal shape + exit path
factors.earns: Bootstrapped or stale/small VC that wants cleanup; majority available; lower-middle-market sell-side bankers (Cascadia, FirstCapital, Vista Point, GrowthPoint, Lincoln, Capstone) are normal counterparties; NA/Europe/Israel HQ with willingness to build a US/Austin presence; a nameable upmarket sponsor (Sumeru, Brighton Park, Francisco, Updata) or strategic at $100-250M in 3-5 years.
factors.loses: VC-shaped rounds (Series A/B, minority-only); strategic auctions run to bundlers; external price anchors (term sheets, SAFE caps); heavy preference stacks or founders under 25%; governance vacuum (no board, CFO, succession); geography outside the box.

rubric.rules: Score = simple average of A-E. Calibration: 75+ chase now; 65-74 real interest with one named blocker; 55-64 only on a specific condition; below 55 pass with the revisit trigger written down. Any factor at 30 or below caps the total at 65, because one broken leg kills these deals in practice. New facts move scores; the rubric does not bend.

pov: Elsewhere Partners is an operating-team transplant business that uses capital as the entry ticket. They buy a time-tested software product (often 7-25 years old) with proven customer pull and a stale or absent go-to-market, install a CEO or Executive Chair from their infrastructure-software bench (SolarWinds, SailPoint, AlienVault alumni), often move HQ to Texas, build a US sales motion, and sell to an upmarket sponsor (Sumeru, Brighton Park, Francisco, Updata) or strategic in 3-5 years at $100-250M. CEO changed in 12 of 21 deals. They are the sole investor in most deals, label them Series A but take control in substance, and buy through lower-middle-market bankers (Cascadia, FirstCapital, Vista Point, GrowthPoint, Lincoln, Capstone). Fund III writes $20-50M majority checks, so the practical ARR floor is about $5M unless a founder secondary is doing the work. Sector results: IT infrastructure/DevOps/monitoring best, then security, then healthcare IT with a bench operator; business applications are their weak vintage. Prior VC is fine when stale and small; live momentum rounds, term sheets, SAFE caps and strategic auctions are disqualifiers. The single strongest signal in their book is product pull without a sales machine.
calibration: CALIBRATION ANCHORS: DarkOwl A75 B90 C75 D85 E80 = 81; MSP Process A90 B55 C85 D80 E70 = 76; Encompaas A80 B70 C60 D85 E75 = 74; Polixis A75 B65 C85 D70 E70 = 73 (verified); CyberDrain A92 B50 C80 D58 E72 = 70 (verified); AlertOps A85 B50 C80 D60 E75 = 70; Competera A70 B75 C40 D65 E25 = 55; DefectDojo A70 B50 C45 D40 E65 = 54 (verified); Espresso AI A60 B40 C55 D30 E40 = 45 (verified); Phin Security A40 B45 C40 D40 E20 = 37

companies.name: Polixis
companies.verifiedNote: Independent verification pass 2026-09-28.
companies.factorReasoning: A: A four-person sales team across London, Geneva and Zurich carrying $5.1M growing 100% is product pull with almost no sales machine, which is the single strongest Elsewhere signal. Four named customer testimonials with titles beat a logo wall, and one (BCP Bank CCO) states they won a competitive parallel bake-off. Five named OEM platform integrations are real embedded distribution the pitch under-sells. Marked down because all 200+ logos are self-reported with no case studies or press, and "Rothschild" is Edmond de Rothschild, a different institution. B: Above the floor with a Rule of 40 of 150 that would be an extreme outlier if true. The unit economics are internally plausible at ~$84k revenue per head with 40+ staff on Armenian salaries. Two problems: the 2023 Swiss balance sheet shows CHF 134k net assets against CHF 1.35M of liabilities, which means the economics sit in Armenia, are swept to the owner annually, or are overstated; and 100% growth alongside 50% EBITDA are in tension unless the Western sales presence really is that thin. C: The best C on the board. The founder has described the Elsewhere model back to them unprompted: majority, operator takes the company, founder goes to product, no earnout. Held below 90 only because he is the sole shareholder with no one forcing a deal, has never sold a company, and his own site claims employee ownership the register contradicts. D: Not a core Elsewhere sector, which caps it, but the durability logic is genuinely strong. Entity resolution against registry data is a data-acquisition problem, not a reasoning problem, and AML is a regime where provenance and audit trail are required, so probabilistic output is not defensible. AMLA standards due July 2026 and the AMLD6 UBO threshold change give a dated demand catalyst inside the hold period. The weakness is that the corpus is assembled from public sources by their own admission. E: Bootstrapped with a sole shareholder is the cleanest cap table the board has seen, geography is in the box, and the exit path is the best documented anywhere in the portfolio: three disclosed strategic comps at 11.6x to 19.5x revenue, plus TPG/Sayari as a structural precedent for exactly this deal. Held at 70 by the absence of a confirmed banker, untested founder motivation, and the employee-equity ambiguity

companies.what: ARDIS platform (not "RAAY" as the pitch states): sanctions, PEPs, RCAs, adverse media, UBO and corporate ownership resolved into one entity-matched graph. Claims 1.9M sanctioned entities, 13M PEP/RCA profiles, 637M corporates and UBOs across 249 jurisdictions, adverse media in 100+ languages. Delivered by REST API, bulk feeds, a graph endpoint, SDKs and an MCP interface. Sister products PEP&REP, CheckMate, Graph AI, AiDA
companies.financials: $5.1M ARR +100%, ~80% ARR / 20% recurring services, 95% GRR, ~50% EBITDA, Rule of 40 of 150 (all founder-stated, nothing public). Bootstrapped; Swiss register confirms Gagik Sargsyan as SOLE shareholder. Polixis SA, CHE-250.050.596, registered Sept 2012, converted Sarl to SA in 2024 (capital CHF 20k to CHF 100k). ~61 FTEs with a 40+ person Yerevan research hub running since 2017
companies.aiTailwinds: Founder explicitly wants a partner to take operational responsibility while he moves to product, explicitly rejects a pure financial buyer or earnout, offering 60/40 majority. Dated regulatory catalyst inside the hold period: EU AMLA operational July 2025, 23 technical standards due 10 July 2026, AMLR and AMLD6 apply 10 July 2027, and the UBO threshold moving from "more than 25%" to "25% or more" forces an EU-wide re-screen of ownership data. Emerging-markets depth (Russia, CIS, Caucasus, MENA) from an Armenian research team is genuinely hard for Moody's or LSEG to replicate and is corroborated on the record by Bank Audi's CCO. Five named OEM integrations (WealthArc, AquaValley BankVista, SpeciTec, Etops, BIGTXN) give embedded distribution. Shipping MCP positions the graph as what agents call rather than what they replace. AML is a defensibility regime: regulators want provenance and audit trail, and a probabilistic model output is not a defensible answer
companies.aiHeadwinds: The corpus is built "exclusively from publicly available sources" by their own account, so a well-funded competitor could re-scrape it; the 637M-entity graph and the emerging-markets depth are the only real moat. LLMs do commoditize the screening interface and adverse-media summarisation. No published false-positive rate, methodology or third-party benchmark anywhere. Their own marketing says the data is "curated and maintained in-house", which is the language of the manual model the pitch claims to be displacing
companies.financialProfile: Above the floor with exceptional stated margins, but the only hard number found (2023 Swiss balance sheet: CHF 134k net assets against CHF 1.35M third-party liabilities) does not look like the home entity of a $5.1M, 50%-margin business
companies.sectorFit: AML/KYC risk data; regulator-driven, consolidating, strong priced exit comps
companies.dealDynamics: Bootstrapped, sole shareholder, no VC to clean up, wants 60/40 growth buyout with $3-5M primary. Switzerland is in the box. Best exit comps on the board: Moody's/Bureau van Dijk at ~11.6x revenue, Moody's/RDC at ~12.7x, Nasdaq/Verafin at ~19.5x, and TPG/Sayari ($235M strategic majority growth investment) is the exact deal shape. No banker confirmed and no evidence AGC holds a mandate
companies.read: Best new name in over a month and the first since DarkOwl that reads like an Elsewhere deal the founder designed himself. Three gating items before anything else: consolidated GROUP accounts plus a QofE, because the Geneva SA alone does not look like the operating entity; the OEM versus direct split of ARR, because embedded data supply into platforms is a materially better revenue shape than selling to Geneva private banks and would make the 95% GRR credible; and resolution of the "100% employee-owned" claim on their own site against a register naming Sargsyan as sole shareholder, which is a change-of-control landmine. Then establish whether AGC actually has a mandate or this is an unmandated conference introduction, because with no investor and no liquidity clock, founder motivation is the whole execution risk
unverified: $5.1M ARR, 100% growth, 50% EBITDA, 95% GRR, Rule of 40 of 150 (nothing public; ZoomInfo estimates under $5M)
